content: Desmocollin-3 is a protein encoded by the DSC3 gene in humans. Members of the desmosomal protein family, including DSC3, are organized into two clusters on chromosome 18, spanning a total of less than 650 kilobases. Alternative splicing of the DSC3 gene results in two distinct transcript variants, which encode different isoforms of the protein. Desmocollin-3 is a calcium-dependent glycoprotein that belongs to the desmocollin subfamily within the cadherin superfamily. These desmosomal proteins, along with desmogleins, are predominantly located in epithelial cells, where they serve as key adhesive components of desmosome cell-cell junctions. They are essential for maintaining cell adhesion and facilitating the formation of desmosomes. A loss of these proteins disrupts cell adhesion, leading to increased cellular mobility. In the context of breast cancer, the expression of desmocollin-3 is frequently downregulated due to epigenetic silencing mechanisms. In a consanguineous Afghan family, hereditary hypotrichosis was observed in three sisters (aged 12 to 18 years) and their 5-year-old brother. This condition was associated with vesicles on the scalp and skin. At birth, the affected individuals had normal scalp hair, which regrew after ritual shaving at one week of age. However, the hair was fragile and began to fall out between 2 to 3 months of age, eventually leaving sparse hair on the scalp. Vesicles, measuring less than 1 cm in diameter, were present on the scalp and other areas of the skin. These vesicles would occasionally disappear and reappear, sometimes rupturing to release fluid and leaving scars that required 3 to 4 months to heal. No mucosal vesicles were observed. Upon clinical examination, the affected individuals exhibited a near absence of eyebrows, eyelashes, axillary hair, and body hair. However, their teeth, nails, palms, soles, sweating, and hearing were normal, as was their electrocardiography. The parents of the affected individuals were clinically unaffected. A scalp biopsy from the 18-year-old sister revealed slight follicular plugging, mild perivascular and periadnexal inflammatory cell infiltration, and normal hair follicles. The sebaceous glands appeared morphologically normal and were connected to the hair follicles. Genotyping and linkage analysis in this family identified a maximum two-point LOD score of 2.68 (theta = 0.0) at markers D18S36 and D18S547. Multipoint analysis yielded a maximum LOD score of 3.30 at marker D18S877. Recombination events defined a critical interval of 8.30 centimorgans on chromosome 18q12.1, flanked by markers D18S66 and D18S1139, which contains 30 genes. A nonsense mutation in the DSC3 gene, located on chromosome 18q12.1, was identified in this family. The mutation, a 2129T-G transversion in exon 14 of the DSC3 gene, results in a substitution of leucine at position 710 with a premature stop codon (L710X). This mutation occurs at the junction of the transmembrane and C-terminal cytoplasmic domains of the protein. It is predicted to cause premature termination of translation, leading to nonsense-mediated decay of the mRNA or instability of the truncated protein. The affected individuals were homozygous for this mutation, while the unaffected parents and three healthy siblings were heterozygous carriers. This mutation was not detected in 100 unrelated ethnically matched controls. Desmocollin-3 has been shown to interact with plakophilin-3 (PKP3).
